# Agent.bx
> **Most agents use Agent.yaml instead**
>
> The default way to define an agent is a plain [`Agent.yaml`](/next/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html). Reach for `Agent.bx` when the definition itself needs code: hooks, dynamic instructions, tools registered in code, an overridden method, or `detectEnvironment()`. A folder holds one or the other, never both. The sections on [the model slug](#the-model-slug), [environment overrides](#environment-overrides), [merge semantics](#merge-semantics) and [the always-on agent route](#the-always-on-agent-route) below apply to both.

`Agent.bx` is the advanced way to define an agent. A BxAgents project needs an `Agent.yaml` **or** an `Agent.bx`. It **extends bx-ai's own [`AiAgent`](https://ai.ortusbooks.com/main-components/agents/class-based-agents)** , so it *is* the agent - the build instantiates it rather than rebuilding one from a config struct, so what you write is what runs. Inherit and add whatever you need: private helpers, overridden methods, tools registered in code. Because it's a real class rather than a struct-returning descriptor, an IDE can introspect it like any other BoxLang class - jump to definition, autocomplete on inherited methods, the works.

```javascript
class extends="bxModules.bxai.models.runnables.AiAgent" {

	function init() {
		super.init(
			name        : "my-agent",
			description : "A helpful assistant",
			instructions: "You are a helpful assistant.",
			model       : aiModel( provider: "openai", params: { model: "gpt-5" } )
		)
		return this
	}

}
```

`bxAgents new --class` scaffolds exactly this shape (without `--class`, `new` scaffolds an `Agent.yaml`). `instructions.md` is optional - set `instructions` directly in `super.init()`, or drop the file beside `Agent.bx` and let the build wire it in for you (see the table below).

## What the build layers on top of the class
> **The rule:** an explicitly declared convention wins; otherwise the class is in charge.

So an agent that sets everything in its own `init()` gets nothing imposed on it, while one that sets the bare minimum still picks up the conventions it didn't speak for. Everything below is **optional** - declare a `configure()` returning any of these keys to override what the class itself set, or the matching `instructions.md`/`tools/`/`subagents/` convention folder:

|                    You declare                    |                                         The build emits                                         |                                                                 If you don't declare it                                                                  |
|---------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `instructions.md`                                 | `withInstructions( fileRead( ... ) )`                                                           | the class's own instructions stand                                                                                                                       |
| `model` in `configure()`                          | `setModel( aiModel( ... ) )`                                                                    | the class's own model stands                                                                                                                             |
| `name` / `description` in `configure()`           | `setName()` / `setDescription()`                                                                | the class's own stand                                                                                                                                    |
| `memory` in `configure()`                         | `setMemory( ... )`                                                                              | the class's own stands                                                                                                                                   |
| the `tools/` folder                               | `withTools( ... )` with that folder's tools                                                     | always - `withTools()` **appends** in bx-ai rather than replacing, so tools your class registered itself are kept and the agent's own `tools/` are added |
| `tools` / `toolOptions` in `configure()`          | `withTools( ... )` with each `item@module` / `*@module` listed, built with the module's options | no module tools; see [Tools](/next/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#tools) and [Tool options](/next/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#tool-options)     |
| `subAgents` on the class, or `subagents/` on disk | `addSubAgent( ... )` per child                                                                  | appended the same way                                                                                                                                    |
| `checkpointer` in `configure()`                   | `withCheckpointer( ... )`                                                                       | **injected anyway** if the class set none - see below                                                                                                    |

> **Info**
>
> The checkpointer is the one thing the build fills in unasked. An agent reachable from a gateway with no checkpointer has *silently* broken human-in-the-loop, so a class that set none still gets the `cache` default. A class that sets its own is left alone.
> **Warning**
>
> Deliberately **not** implemented by comparing your instance against bx-ai's `DEFAULT_AGENT_*` values. "Did the author mean this, or is it just the default?" is unanswerable, and an author who genuinely wanted the default name would find it silently replaced. Presence of an external declaration is a fact; intent behind a default value is not.

The class is copied into the generated app at `agent/classes/` and instantiated there by its own absolute file path (never a relative lookup that would depend on a registered mapping), exactly as `tools/`, `skills/` and `mcp/` are copied - so a packaged `.bxa` carries it, and `chat`/`invoke`/`serve` all instantiate it the same way whether or not a real ColdBox container is booted.

## `configure()` (optional) - overriding what the class set

A `configure()` method is entirely optional. Declare it only to override specific fields from outside the class - useful for keeping deployment-specific values (a different model per environment, say) out of the class body itself:

```javascript
class extends="bxModules.bxai.models.runnables.AiAgent" {

	function init() {
		super.init(
			name  : "with-mcp-servers-agent",
			model : aiModel( provider: "openai", params: { model: "gpt-5" } )
		)
		return this
	}

	function configure() {
		return {
			mcpServers : [
				"https://example.com/mcp",
				{ url : "https://other.com/mcp", name : "other" }
			]
		};
	}

}
```

|      Field       |       Type       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|------------------|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `name`           | string           | Also becomes this agent's `config/WireBox.bx` binding key at build time (`getInstance( name )`) - see [schedules/](/next/conventions/schedules/index.html) - so it must be unique across the whole project (root + every subagent); `build` fails if two agents share a name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `model`          | string           | A `provider/model` slug or a bare provider name. A `profile` (see [Models and profiles](/next/conventions/models/index.html)) can stand in for it. See below.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `description`    | string           | Optional.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `subAgents`      | array of strings | Names of sibling folders under the root project's `subagents/`. See [subagents/](/next/conventions/subagents/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `mcpServers`     | array            | Remote MCP servers - each entry a URL string or `{ url, name }`. See [mcp/](/next/conventions/mcp/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `security`       | struct           | Forwarded verbatim into the generated app's `bxai` module settings; bx-ai's own `SecurityDirector` turns it into guardrail middleware. Passthrough only - BxAgents has no own guardrails convention.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `memory`         | string or struct | The agent's conversation memory. A bare string is shorthand for the type (`"cache"`); a struct is `{ type, ...config }` and is passed through to `aiMemory()` verbatim - e.g. `{ type: "cache", maxMessages: 50 }`, or with `summaryProvider`/`summaryModel`/`summaryThreshold` to make the web UI's `/compact` functional. Applies per node, so a subagent can declare its own.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `checkpointer`   | struct           | `{ type: "cache"\|"file"\|"jdbc", ...config }`. Defaults to `{ type: "cache" }` if omitted. Always applied - without one, human-in-the-loop approval flows through any gateway other than `cli` fail outright.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `gatewaySession` | struct           | `{ policy, maxQueueDepth, commands }`, all optional (default `"queue"` / `50` / a safe set of [slash commands](/next/conventions/gateways/index.html#commands-in-a-gateway)). Only meaningful if the project has at least one push-style [gateway](/next/conventions/gateways/index.html#3-push-style-gateways-type-telegram--slack--discord--email--whatsapp-cloud--teams--twilio--github--signal-and-friends) entry - controls the generated `GatewaySession`'s policy for a second inbound message arriving on a thread that already has a turn in flight. `policy` must be one of `reject`/`queue`/`steer`/`interrupt`. |
| `agentApi`       | struct           | `{ enabled, tokenEnvVar, tokens, profiles }`, all optional. Controls the always-on agent route at `/__bxagents`. See [The always-on agent route](#the-always-on-agent-route) below.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| any other key    | any              | Merged and available in the resolved config struct, but not interpreted by BxAgents itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

## The model slug

`model` is BxAgents' own convention - bx-ai itself takes `provider` and `model` as two separate arguments to `aiModel()`. BxAgents splits the slug **on the first `/` only** , so a provider that itself contains a slash (like OpenRouter's `openrouter/anthropic/claude-x`) still parses correctly:

|          `model` value          |   provider   |        model         |
|---------------------------------|--------------|----------------------|
| `openai/gpt-5`                  | `openai`     | `gpt-5`              |
| `openrouter/anthropic/claude-x` | `openrouter` | `anthropic/claude-x` |
| `mock/mock-model`               | `mock`       | `mock-model`         |

If `model` has no `/` at all, it must be a known core provider name (the provider's default model) - validation rejects anything else. The recognized core providers are: `bedrock`, `cartesia`, `claude`, `cloudflare`, `cohere`, `deepseek`, `docker`, `elevenlabs`, `gemini`, `grok`, `groq`, `huggingface`, `minimax`, `mistral`, `mock`, `ollama`, `openai`, `openai-compatible`, `openrouter`, `perplexity`, `voyage` (kept in sync with bx-ai's own `CORE_PROVIDERS`). `mock` is a real provider, useful for tests and CI - it never makes a network call.

This slug-splitting convention is what a `configure()`-declared `model` string goes through - `super.init()`'s own `model` argument instead takes a real `AiModel` instance directly (`aiModel( provider: "...", params: { model: "..." } )`), since the class already speaks bx-ai's own API.

## Environment overrides

`Agent.bx` may declare a method named after an environment (e.g. `production()`, `development()`, or any custom name) returning a struct of overrides - this works whether or not the class also declares a `configure()`:

```javascript
class extends="bxModules.bxai.models.runnables.AiAgent" {

	function init() {
		super.init(
			name        : "override-agent",
			description : "An agent with an environment override",
			model       : aiModel( provider: "openai", params: { model: "gpt-5" } )
		)
		return this
	}

	function production() {
		return {
			model : "openai/gpt-5-mini"
		};
	}

}
```

The active environment is resolved with this precedence (highest wins):

1. `--environment` CLI flag (`bxAgents build --environment=production`)
2. `Agent.bx`'s own `detectEnvironment()` method, if it declares one
3. `BX_AGENTS_ENV` environment variable
4. `"development"` (default)

### `detectEnvironment()`

For anything the first and third tiers can't express, `Agent.bx` may declare a
`detectEnvironment()` method and decide for itself. Whatever it returns is taken
as the environment name verbatim:

```javascript
class extends="bxModules.bxai.models.runnables.AiAgent" {

	function init() {
		super.init( name : "my-agent", model : aiModel( provider : "openai", params : { model : "gpt-5" } ) )
		return this
	}

	function detectEnvironment() {
		return fileExists( expandPath( "/.production-marker" ) ) ? "production" : "development";
	}

}
```

This mirrors ColdBox's own tier-1 convention (a config declaring
`detectEnvironment()` has its return value taken verbatim), with two deliberate
differences, both because this runs at **build** time:

* An explicit `--environment` flag **outranks** `detectEnvironment()` here, where ColdBox puts its own detect method first. A flag someone typed is the most specific statement of intent available.
* ColdBox's *other* detection tier - an `environments` struct of regexes matched against `CGI.HTTP_HOST` - is **not** supported. It cannot work here: the build runs in a CLI process with no HTTP host, so it would only ever describe the machine doing the building (a CI runner would resolve `development` for a production build).

Returning a blank string, or anything that isn't a string, means "no opinion" and
falls through to the next tier - so a project computing its environment from
something absent on this machine degrades to the default rather than failing the
build. A `detectEnvironment()` that **throws** is a different matter: that's a real
bug in the project's own code, and `build` fails and says so.

This is a **build-time** decision only, distinct from ColdBox's own runtime environment detection (the generated app reads `getSetting("environment")` on its own, per ColdBox's `environments` convention) - this precedence only decides which `environment()` override method on `Agent.bx`, and which `boxlang-{env}.json`/`miniserver-{env}.json` files, the build pipeline applies.

If no method matching the active environment exists, no override is applied.

## Merge semantics

The full resolution order (lowest to highest precedence) is:

1. `configure()` (optional)
2. the matching environment-override method, if any
3. `boxlang.json`
4. `boxlang-{environment}.json`
5. `miniserver.json`
6. `miniserver-{environment}.json`

Struct keys are merged **recursively** - a nested struct in a higher-precedence source only overrides the keys it actually sets, leaving sibling keys from a lower-precedence source intact. Arrays and all scalar values are **replaced whole**, never appended or concatenated.

`boxlang.json`/`boxlang-{env}.json`/`miniserver.json`/`miniserver-{env}.json` are all optional project-root JSON files, useful for config that's easier to express as data than as BoxLang code (e.g. model defaults):

```json
// boxlang.json
{
	"modelDefaults": { "temperature": 0.7, "maxTokens": 1000 }
}
```

```json
// boxlang-production.json
{
	"modelDefaults": { "temperature": 0.2 }
}
```

Building with `--environment=production` here yields `modelDefaults: { temperature: 0.2, maxTokens: 1000 }` - the recursive merge kept `maxTokens` from the base file since `boxlang-production.json` never mentioned it.
> **Warning**
>
> Secrets (API keys, tokens) are never read or merged by BxAgents at build time - they stay external (an OS environment variable, `.env`, a platform secret manager) and are resolved live by bx-ai itself at runtime. See [Deployment \& Secrets](/next/deployment-and-secrets/index.html).

## The always-on agent route

Every built project exposes its root agent over HTTP at a fixed reserved path,
whether or not it declares any [`gateways/`](/next/conventions/gateways/index.html) entries:

    POST /__bxagents/invoke
    POST /__bxagents/stream    # SSE
    POST /__bxagents/batch
    GET  /__bxagents/info

These are the four sub-routes ColdBox's own `toAi()` terminator registers. The
route exists so this module's own tooling always has an address to talk to -
it's the service entrance, not your project's public API. A project's own
public surface belongs in `gateways/`, at whatever paths you choose.

### Run control

Beside those four, a generated handler (`handlers/AgentApi.bx`) serves what a chat client needs to
control a run. It is what `chat --server` and `chat --connect` use:

    POST /__bxagents/events    # SSE: like /stream, plus tool and suspended frames. Body may carry
                               # attachments: [ { name, mime, data (base64) } ], at most 4 pictures of 5 MB
    POST /__bxagents/cancel    # { threadId, reason? }
    POST /__bxagents/steer     # { threadId, input }
    GET  /__bxagents/pending   # ?threadId=
    POST /__bxagents/resume    # { threadId, decision } -> SSE, like /events
    GET  /__bxagents/tools
    GET  /__bxagents/profiles   # the profiles a client may ask for
    GET  /__bxagents/agent    # name, model, what it can do
    GET  /__bxagents/sessions   # the caller's recent conversations
    POST /__bxagents/sessions/rename   # { conversationId, title } name one
    POST /__bxagents/sessions/fork     # { conversationId, title? } copy one, messages and all
    GET  /__bxagents/history    # ?conversationId= what was said in one
    POST /__bxagents/clear      # { conversationId } forget its messages
    POST /__bxagents/compact    # { conversationId } summarize the older messages
    POST /__bxagents/ping       # { profile? } test a model with one tiny question: { ok, model, ms, reply } or { ok : false, model, reason }
    GET  /__bxagents/commands   # the slash commands this caller may run, [ { name, hint } ]
    GET  /__bxagents/context    # ?conversationId= estimated size of the context: parts, largest tools, total, share of the window
    POST /__bxagents/command    # { line : "/info", conversationId? } run one, answers { blocks, effects, conversationId }
    GET  /__bxagents/notes    # the caller's notes and the agent's, with how full they are
    POST /__bxagents/notes    # { scope : "user" | "agent", text }
    POST /__bxagents/notes/update   # { scope, id, text }
    POST /__bxagents/notes/remove   # { scope, id }

`/events` sends the frames of `/stream` (`thread` first, `chunk` for each piece of the answer, `done` last)
and adds:

|    Frame    |                                                      Data                                                      |
|-------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `tool`      | `{ id, name, arguments, status, ms }`, once with `status: "running"` and once with `"ok"` and the time it took |
| `suspended` | `{ threadId, pendingActions : [ { toolName, toolArgs } ] }` when the run waits for a human decision            |
| `error`     | `{ message }`                                                                                                  |

`cancel` stops the run at its next checkpoint (before the next model call or tool call, not in the middle of
a token). `steer` splices a message into a run in flight. `resume` takes `approve`, `approve_session` or
`reject` and streams the rest of the turn. A run belongs to whoever started it: `pending` answers "nothing
pending" and `resume` answers `403` to anyone else.

Send a `conversationId` with `/events` to keep the turn in a conversation: the server lists it under the caller (the name of the token used, or `api` on an open route) and the agent's memory keeps its messages under the same id. `sessions`, `history`, `clear` and `compact` work on the caller's own conversations only; someone else's id is a `404`, the same as one that does not exist. They answer `404` when the server has no shared chat database, and `compact` reports `available: false` when the agent's memory has no summary model.

The `notes` routes answer `404` for an agent that has no [`notes`](/next/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#notes) block. Each caller reads and changes their own user notes (the owner is the name of the token they used, or `api` on an open route) and the agent's notes. Any caller can add to either scope or edit a note; removing a note of the agent needs an `admin` token (a `403` otherwise), because it changes what every user's agent knows.

These routes sit behind the same `x-bxagents-token` gate as the other four (a missing or wrong token is a
`401`), and `agentApi.enabled: false` removes all of them.

Because the path is reserved, `build` **rejects** any `gateways/` entry whose
`path` is `/__bxagents` or sits underneath it. Two routes on one mount is a
genuine conflict: one would silently shadow the other, and yours would be the
one that never answers.

### `agentApi`

`configure()` may return an `agentApi` struct to control it:

|      Key      |  Type   |                                                                                                                                                                                          Notes                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|---------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `enabled`     | boolean | Default `true`. Set `false` to omit the route entirely - for a build going somewhere it has no business existing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `tokenEnvVar` | string  | The **name** of an environment variable holding a shared secret. When set, every sub-route requires a matching `x-bxagents-token` request header.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `tokens`      | boolean | Default `false`. `true` also accepts the [access tokens](#access-tokens-for-a-deployed-agent) made with `bxAgents token create`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `profiles`    | list    | Default none. The [profiles](/next/conventions/models/index.html#profiles) a client may ask for with `options.profile` on `/events`, and what `GET /__bxagents/profiles` lists (never a key). Any other profile is a `400`, so a caller cannot pick a model you did not offer. `chat --connect` uses this list for `/profile`. Each name must be declared in `Agent.yaml`, or `default`. |

```javascript
function configure() {
	return {
		name     : "my-agent",
		model    : "openai/gpt-5",
		agentApi : {
			tokenEnvVar : "BXAGENTS_API_TOKEN"
		}
	};
}
```

Because this comes from `configure()`, it scopes per environment with an
[environment override](#environment-overrides) like any other key - so a
project can leave the route open locally and require a token in production:

```javascript
function production() {
	return {
		agentApi : { tokenEnvVar : "BXAGENTS_API_TOKEN" }
	};
}
```

The gate **fails closed** : if the named variable is unset or blank at runtime,
nothing matches - it never degenerates into comparing `""` to `""` and letting
every caller through. A request without a valid token gets a `401` with a small
JSON body, and never reaches the agent.
> **Warning**
>
> `tokenEnvVar` names a **variable** , never the secret itself. `build` rejects
> a value that isn't a valid environment-variable name, precisely so a literal
> token can't be committed here by mistake. Only the variable's name is ever
> written into generated source.

### Access tokens for a deployed agent

One shared secret (`tokenEnvVar`) is enough for a single caller. To let several people or machines in, each with a name you can revoke, turn on issued tokens:

```yaml
# Agent.yaml
agentApi:
  tokens: true
```

Make them where the agent's database is: on the server, or in the project before you pack it.

```bash
bxAgents token create --name=laptop --expires=90d
bxAgents token create --name=ci --scope=admin
bxAgents token list
bxAgents token revoke --name=laptop
```

* A token is shown **once**, when it is made. Only its SHA-256 is stored, so a stolen database file cannot be used to call the agent.
* The caller sends it in the `x-bxagents-token` header, or `bxAgents chat --connect=<url> --token=<token>` (or `BXAGENTS_TOKEN`) does.
* The name is who is calling. A run belongs to the token that started it, and one token cannot answer another's pending approval. The scope is `chat` or `admin`.
* Revoking takes effect on the next request, without a restart. A token can also expire (`--expires=90d`, `12h`, `2w` or a date).
* With `tokens: true` and no `tokenEnvVar`, a server with no tokens yet refuses everyone. With both, the shared secret works as an `admin` token, so a fresh deployment can be reached before the first token exists.
* The tokens live in the [shared chat database](/next/conventions/web-ui/index.html#the-sqlite-store) (`data/chat.db`). On a deployed server run `token` with `BXAGENTS_DB` pointing at the file the app uses.

Put HTTPS in front of any server a token travels to: a token on plain HTTP can be read on the wire.
> **Info**
>
> The route is bound to whatever host the [miniserver](/next/cli-reference/index.html#serve)
> is listening on - `127.0.0.1` by default, so nothing is reachable off the
> machine unless you deliberately expose it. `tokenEnvVar` is what matters once
> you do, and for any built `.bxa` artifact you deploy.

body: Agent.yaml Agent.yaml is the default way to define an agent. It is a plain YAML file - a name, a model, and any of the optional settings below - and the build turns it into a running agent. Most agents need nothing more than this file and an instructions.md beside it. name: support description: Answers customer questions about orders model: openai/gpt-5 environments: test: model: mock/mock-model bxAgents new scaffolds exactly this shape. When the definition needs real code (hooks, dynamic instructions, tools registered in code), use the advanced option instead: a class-based Agent.bx , scaffolded with bxAgents new --class . Info A folder holds one agent definition. An Agent.yaml (or Agent.yml ) together with an Agent.bx in the same folder is an error - two definitions of one agent would leave it ambiguous which settings win - and build fails and names both files so you can keep one. This applies to the project root and to every subagent folder, and a project can mix the two: a YAML root with a class-based subagent, or the other way round. Settings Key Type Notes name string Also becomes this agent's config/WireBox.bx binding key at build time, so it must be unique across the whole project (root + every subagent). model string A provider/model slug, a bare provider name, or a model name when provider is set. See The model slug and Models and profiles . provider string The default provider, a bx-ai provider name. With model as a bare model name. See Models and profiles . params mapping Default request parameters, such as temperature . options mapping Default provider options, such as timeout . providers mapping Per provider params and options , by provider name. profiles mapping Named combinations of provider, model, params, options and apiKeyEnv , and optionally contextWindow and vision . contextWindow , vision number, boolean What the default model can hold (tokens) and whether it can see images. Optional facts for the chat; bx-ai does not read them. See Models . defaultProfile string The profile used when nothing asks for another. profile string The profile this agent uses. embeddings , speech , transcription , image mapping bx-ai's capability defaults: provider , model and a few settings each. description string Optional. instructions string Optional inline instructions. See Instructions . tools list of strings Module tools this agent gets, as item@module or *@module . See Tools . toolOptions mapping Options for a module's tools, keyed by module name. See Tool options . subAgents list of strings Names of sibling folders under the root project's subagents/ . See subagents/ . mcpServers list MCP servers - each entry a URL string, a mapping with url and the credentials the server wants ( token , headers , timeout ), or a mapping with command for a server that runs as a program ( env , cwd , prefix , toolFilter ). See mcp/ . security mapping Forwarded verbatim into the generated app's bxai module settings; bx-ai's own SecurityDirector turns it into guardrail middleware. memory string or mapping The agent's conversation memory. A bare string is the type ( cache ); a mapping is { type, ...config } and is passed through to aiMemory() . A memory is keyed by the agent's name, so one that is kept on disk is found again on the next start; set key in the mapping to name it yourself. checkpointer mapping { type: cache\|file\|jdbc, ...config } . Defaults to { type: cache } if omitted. gatewaySession mapping { policy, maxQueueDepth, commands } , all optional. See Agent.bx for the values; they are identical. agentApi mapping { enabled, tokenEnvVar, tokens, profiles } , all optional. See The always-on agent route . notes mapping Short notes the agent keeps about the user and its own work. notes: {} turns them on with the defaults. See Notes . usage boolean Records what each model call used (the time, who, the provider, the model and the tokens), for bxAgents stats and /stats . Off by default : set usage: true to turn it on. Counts only, never what was said. Only in the project's own Agent.yaml . Rebuild after changing it. tui mapping How the terminal chat looks: { prompt, widgets: { top, bottom } } , all optional. prompt is bars (default), bars-hints , rule , box or panel ; widgets list what goes in the top bar and at the bottom ( agent , profile , folder , user , clock , machine , git , date , session , elapsed , ctx ). A wrong name is refused and the valid ones are listed. Only in the project's own Agent.yaml . See The prompt and the tables . extensions mapping Values for the project's extensions , by extension name, and what to turn off: { disable: [ roll, "deploy:deploy" ], deploy: { target: production } } . Each extension's block is merged over the defaults its configure() sets. Only in the project's own Agent.yaml . environments mapping Per-environment overrides. See Environments . These are the same settings an Agent.bx 's configure() returns, so every behavior documented for them applies unchanged. Warning An unknown key is an error , and the message lists the valid ones. A typo such as modle: would otherwise do nothing, quietly. Settings that arrive in later releases (for example mcp ) are rejected the same way until they exist, rather than being silently ignored. Anything free-form belongs in an Agent.bx . A value of the wrong type (a text where a list belongs, say) and an empty value ( model: with nothing after it) are errors too. Tools An agent gets its own tools/ folder, and nothing else, unless it asks. The tools other modules provide (bx-ai's built-ins, bx-playwright , ...) are a catalog: they are available, but an agent only has the ones its tools: list names. Every entry is item@module , the key bx-ai keeps them under: name: support model: openai/gpt-5 tools: - now@bxai # one tool from one module - "*@bxplaywright" # every tool that module registered (quote it: * starts a YAML alias) Entry Gives the agent item@module that one tool *@module , or @module every tool the module registered Default. No tools: means only the agent's own tools/ . This holds for every subagent too: each one has its own tools/ and its own tools: . Naming a module validates it. If the module is not installed, or has no such tool, build and the generated app fail with a message that lists what the module does provide. A bare name is an error. now fails with a hint to write now@bxai . bx-ai would otherwise resolve it to whichever module registered a tool called now first. Own tools win. If a tool in the agent's tools/ has the same name as a module tool it selected, the own tool is used and the module tool is left out, with a warning in the bxagents-tools log. Each tool once. Listing a tool twice, or listing it along with a *@module that covers it, attaches it once. Tool options toolOptions configures the tools of a module, keyed by module name . Two modules take options: bxai , for its file tools , and bxplaywright , whose options are those of bx-playwright's playwright() : a profile (a name, or a list of names) and settings such as headless , baseURL , browser , viewport or device . tools: - "*@bxplaywright" toolOptions: bxplaywright: profile: mobile headless: false baseURL: ${env.APP_URL:http://localhost:8080} Each agent gets its own browser. The browser tools bx-playwright registers share one browser for the whole app. An agent that lists bxplaywright tools does not get those: it gets a fresh set built for it alone ( playwright( profile, options ).aiTools() ), so a root agent and its subagent never drive the same page. The browser opens when one of its tools is first used, not at startup. *@bxplaywright works with no toolOptions at all and uses the module's own settings. Environment values. ${env.NAME}` and `${env.NAME:default} are replaced with the environment variable when the app starts, never at build time, so a secret or a per-machine setting stays out of the project. A variable that is not set and has no default fails the agent at startup, naming it. Checked at build time. A key that is not a module the agent lists tools from, a module that takes no options, a key written as item@module , or an option bx-playwright does not have (the message lists the valid ones) is a build error. The module-wide settings (where browsers are installed, the default profile) stay in bx-playwright's own settings, not here. File tools bx-ai has 19 file tools ( readFile , writeFile , listDirectory , searchFiles , deleteFile , zipFiles and more), but it registers none of them. In BxAgents an agent gets them by listing them and naming the folders they may use in toolOptions.bxai.allowedPaths : tools: - readFile@bxai - listDirectory@bxai toolOptions: bxai: allowedPaths: - tmp # the system temp folder - cwd # the folder the agent is started from - /data/reports # or an absolute path Each agent gets its own tools, locked to its own folders. A path outside them is refused ( .. tricks included), and the tools are never put in the shared registry where another agent could pick them up. No folders, no tools. The tools exist only when allowedPaths is set, and an empty list is a build error, because bx-ai reads an empty list as "any path". Listing readFile@bxai with no allowedPaths fails with a message saying so. now@bxai , httpGet@bxai , webSearch@bxai and the rest of bx-ai's registered tools keep working as before, with or without toolOptions.bxai . *@bxai includes the file tools once allowedPaths is set. An entry may be ${env.NAME} to take a folder from the environment. bxAgents new can write all of this for you: see the new wizard . Notes An agent can keep short notes: things about the user ("prefers short answers") and things about its own work ("the repo uses Gradle"). They are off until the block is there: notes: {} notes: provider: sqlite # built in. Or a class implementing INotesProvider user: { limit: 1400 } # characters of user notes that go into the prompt agent: { limit: 2200 } # characters of agent notes tool: true # give the agent the remember and forget tools (default true) approveForget: true # a person approves what the agent forgets (default true) Key Default Notes provider sqlite sqlite keeps one row per note in the shared chat database . Any other value is the name of a class that implements INotesProvider and is created with ( config, agentName ) , for a notes service of your own. user.limit 1400 Characters of notes about the user. Each user has their own. agent.limit 2200 Characters of notes about the agent's work. Shared by everyone who talks to it. tool true remember (save or replace a note) and forget (remove one). Without them the notes are read-only for the agent and a person manages them. approveForget true A run that wants to forget stops for approval , like any tool that needs it. Saving a note needs none. How it works: Both scopes go into the system prompt as short lists, oldest first, within their limits. They are read once per conversation, so the prompt stays the same turn to turn (a provider's prompt cache keeps working) and a note saved now shows from the next conversation. A note is one line of at most 500 characters. Nothing is dropped silently: a note that does not fit the limit is refused, and the agent is told how full the notes are so it can replace or forget an older one. Who a user is : in bxAgents chat it is the operating system user ( --user=NAME changes it); on a server it is the name of the access token the caller used, or api when the route is open. The agent scope belongs to the agent's name . The terminal chat, the web chat and the server share one file, data/chat.db (see the SQLite store ). Manage them yourself with /remember and /notes in chat , with bxAgents notes from a shell, or over HTTP through the run-control routes . Instructions The agent's instructions are its system prompt. Put them in an instructions.md beside Agent.yaml , the usual choice because the file is plain Markdown and easy to edit: my-agent/ ├── Agent.yaml └── instructions.md For a short prompt you can write them inline instead: name: greeter model: openai/gpt-5 instructions: | You greet people by name. Keep it to one sentence. If both exist, instructions.md wins - the file is the more deliberate choice, so a stray instructions: line cannot override it. If neither exists, build fails and says so. Environments environments holds overrides keyed by environment name. It is the YAML spelling of the environment-override methods ( production() ) an Agent.bx can declare: name: support model: openai/gpt-5 environments: production: model: openai/gpt-5-mini staging: description: Staging copy The active environment is chosen with this precedence, highest first: the --environment CLI flag ( bxAgents build --environment=production ) the BX_AGENTS_ENV environment variable development Only the block for the active environment is applied, on top of the top-level settings; keys it does not mention are left alone. Each block accepts the same keys as the top level, except environments itself. bxAgents test builds against the test environment, which is why a scaffolded project carries a test block pointing at the mock provider: its tests need no API key or network access. Note An Agent.yaml cannot compute its environment. The detectEnvironment() method described under Environment overrides needs code, so a project that needs it uses an Agent.bx . The overrides then merge with boxlang.json , boxlang-{environment}.json , miniserver.json and miniserver-{environment}.json exactly as described in Merge semantics . Requirements Reading YAML needs the bx-yaml module, 1.1.0 or later . BxAgents bundles it, so there is nothing to install. Global YAML tags (such as !!java.io.File ) are rejected, so a cloned project's Agent.yaml cannot make the build instantiate arbitrary Java classes. YAML or Agent.bx? Use When Agent.yaml The agent is configuration: a name, a model, instructions, memory, subagents. This is almost every agent. Agent.bx The definition itself needs code: hooks, dynamic instructions, tools registered in code, an overridden method, or detectEnvironment() . You can start with YAML and switch later: create the Agent.bx , move the settings across, and delete the Agent.yaml .

# Agent.yaml

`Agent.yaml` is the default way to define an agent. It is a plain YAML file - a name, a model, and any of the optional settings below - and the build turns it into a running agent. Most agents need nothing more than this file and an [`instructions.md`](#instructions) beside it.

```yaml
name: support
description: Answers customer questions about orders
model: openai/gpt-5

environments:
  test:
    model: mock/mock-model
```

`bxAgents new` scaffolds exactly this shape. When the definition needs real code (hooks, dynamic instructions, tools registered in code), use the advanced option instead: a class-based [`Agent.bx`](/next/conventions/agent-bx/index.html), scaffolded with `bxAgents new --class`.
> **Info**
>
> A folder holds **one** agent definition. An `Agent.yaml` (or `Agent.yml`) together with an `Agent.bx` in the same folder is an error - two definitions of one agent would leave it ambiguous which settings win - and `build` fails and names both files so you can keep one. This applies to the project root and to every [subagent](/next/conventions/subagents/index.html) folder, and a project can mix the two: a YAML root with a class-based subagent, or the other way round.

## Settings

|                       Key                        |       Type        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------------------------------------|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `name`                                           | string            | Also becomes this agent's `config/WireBox.bx` binding key at build time, so it must be unique across the whole project (root + every subagent).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `model`                                          | string            | A `provider/model` slug, a bare provider name, or a model name when `provider` is set. See [The model slug](/next/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#the-model-slug) and [Models and profiles](/next/conventions/models/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `provider`                                       | string            | The default provider, a bx-ai provider name. With `model` as a bare model name. See [Models and profiles](/next/conventions/models/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `params`                                         | mapping           | Default request parameters, such as `temperature`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `options`                                        | mapping           | Default provider options, such as `timeout`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `providers`                                      | mapping           | Per provider `params` and `options`, by provider name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `profiles`                                       | mapping           | Named combinations of provider, model, params, options and `apiKeyEnv`, and optionally `contextWindow` and `vision`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `contextWindow`, `vision`                        | number, boolean   | What the default model can hold (tokens) and whether it can see images. Optional facts for the chat; bx-ai does not read them. See [Models](/next/conventions/models/index.html#what-the-project-knows-about-a-model).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `defaultProfile`                                 | string            | The profile used when nothing asks for another.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `profile`                                        | string            | The profile this agent uses.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `embeddings`, `speech`, `transcription`, `image` | mapping           | bx-ai's capability defaults: `provider`, `model` and a few settings each.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `description`                                    | string            | Optional.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `instructions`                                   | string            | Optional inline instructions. See [Instructions](#instructions).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `tools`                                          | list of strings   | Module tools this agent gets, as `item@module` or `*@module`. See [Tools](#tools).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `toolOptions`                                    | mapping           | Options for a module's tools, keyed by module name. See [Tool options](#tool-options).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `subAgents`                                      | list of strings   | Names of sibling folders under the root project's `subagents/`. See [subagents/](/next/conventions/subagents/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `mcpServers`                                     | list              | MCP servers - each entry a URL string, a mapping with `url` and the credentials the server wants (`token`, `headers`, `timeout`), or a mapping with `command` for a server that runs as a program (`env`, `cwd`, `prefix`, `toolFilter`). See [mcp/](/next/conventions/mcp/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `security`                                       | mapping           | Forwarded verbatim into the generated app's `bxai` module settings; bx-ai's own `SecurityDirector` turns it into guardrail middleware.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `memory`                                         | string or mapping | The agent's conversation memory. A bare string is the type (`cache`); a mapping is `{ type, ...config }` and is passed through to `aiMemory()`. A memory is keyed by the agent's name, so one that is kept on disk is found again on the next start; set `key` in the mapping to name it yourself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `checkpointer`                                   | mapping           | `{ type: cache\|file\|jdbc, ...config }`. Defaults to `{ type: cache }` if omitted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `gatewaySession`                                 | mapping           | `{ policy, maxQueueDepth, commands }`, all optional. See [Agent.bx](/next/conventions/agent-bx/index.html) for the values; they are identical.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `agentApi`                                       | mapping           | `{ enabled, tokenEnvVar, tokens, profiles }`, all optional. See [The always-on agent route](/next/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#the-always-on-agent-route).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `notes`                                          | mapping           | Short notes the agent keeps about the user and its own work. `notes: {}` turns them on with the defaults. See [Notes](#notes).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `usage`                                          | boolean           | Records what each model call used (the time, who, the provider, the model and the tokens), for [`bxAgents stats`](/next/cli-reference/index.html#stats) and `/stats`. **Off by default** : set `usage: true` to turn it on. Counts only, never what was said. Only in the project's own `Agent.yaml`. Rebuild after changing it.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `tui`                                            | mapping           | How the terminal chat looks: `{ prompt, widgets: { top, bottom } }`, all optional. `prompt` is `bars` (default), `bars-hints`, `rule`, `box` or `panel`; `widgets` list what goes in the top bar and at the bottom (`agent`, `profile`, `folder`, `user`, `clock`, `machine`, `git`, `date`, `session`, `elapsed`, `ctx`). A wrong name is refused and the valid ones are listed. Only in the project's own `Agent.yaml`. See [The prompt and the tables](/next/cli-reference/index.html#the-prompt-and-the-tables). |
| `extensions`                                     | mapping           | Values for the project's [extensions](/next/conventions/extensions/index.html), by extension name, and what to turn off: `{ disable: [ roll, "deploy:deploy" ], deploy: { target: production } }`. Each extension's block is merged over the defaults its `configure()` sets. Only in the project's own `Agent.yaml`.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `environments`                                   | mapping           | Per-environment overrides. See [Environments](#environments).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

These are the same settings an `Agent.bx`'s `configure()` returns, so every behavior documented for them applies unchanged.
> **Warning**
>
> An **unknown key is an error** , and the message lists the valid ones. A typo such as `modle:` would otherwise do nothing, quietly. Settings that arrive in later releases (for example `mcp`) are rejected the same way until they exist, rather than being silently ignored. Anything free-form belongs in an `Agent.bx`.

A value of the wrong type (a text where a list belongs, say) and an empty value (`model:` with nothing after it) are errors too.

## Tools

An agent gets its own `tools/` folder, and nothing else, unless it asks. The tools other modules provide (bx-ai's built-ins, `bx-playwright`, ...) are a catalog: they are available, but an agent only has the ones its `tools:` list names. Every entry is `item@module`, the key bx-ai keeps them under:

```yaml
name: support
model: openai/gpt-5
tools:
  - now@bxai            # one tool from one module
  - "*@bxplaywright"    # every tool that module registered (quote it: * starts a YAML alias)
```

|          Entry           |         Gives the agent          |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------|
| `item@module`            | that one tool                    |
| `*@module`, or `@module` | every tool the module registered |

* **Default.** No `tools:` means only the agent's own `tools/`. This holds for every [subagent](/next/conventions/subagents/index.html) too: each one has its own `tools/` and its own `tools:`.
* **Naming a module validates it.** If the module is not installed, or has no such tool, `build` and the generated app fail with a message that lists what the module does provide.
* **A bare name is an error.** `now` fails with a hint to write `now@bxai`. bx-ai would otherwise resolve it to whichever module registered a tool called `now` first.
* **Own tools win.** If a tool in the agent's `tools/` has the same name as a module tool it selected, the own tool is used and the module tool is left out, with a warning in the `bxagents-tools` log.
* **Each tool once.** Listing a tool twice, or listing it along with a `*@module` that covers it, attaches it once.

### Tool options

`toolOptions` configures the tools of a module, keyed by **module name** . Two modules take options: `bxai`, for its [file tools](#file-tools), and `bxplaywright`, whose options are those of bx-playwright's `playwright()`: a `profile` (a name, or a list of names) and settings such as `headless`, `baseURL`, `browser`, `viewport` or `device`.

```yaml
tools:
  - "*@bxplaywright"
toolOptions:
  bxplaywright:
    profile: mobile
    headless: false
    baseURL: ${env.APP_URL:http://localhost:8080}
```

* **Each agent gets its own browser.** The browser tools bx-playwright registers share one browser for the whole app. An agent that lists `bxplaywright` tools does not get those: it gets a fresh set built for it alone (`playwright( profile, options ).aiTools()`), so a root agent and its subagent never drive the same page. The browser opens when one of its tools is first used, not at startup. `*@bxplaywright` works with no `toolOptions` at all and uses the module's own settings.
* **Environment values.** ``${env.NAME}` and `${env.NAME:default}`` are replaced with the environment variable when the app starts, never at build time, so a secret or a per-machine setting stays out of the project. A variable that is not set and has no default fails the agent at startup, naming it.
* **Checked at build time.** A key that is not a module the agent lists tools from, a module that takes no options, a key written as `item@module`, or an option bx-playwright does not have (the message lists the valid ones) is a `build` error.
* The module-wide settings (where browsers are installed, the default profile) stay in bx-playwright's own settings, not here.

### File tools

bx-ai has 19 file tools (`readFile`, `writeFile`, `listDirectory`, `searchFiles`, `deleteFile`, `zipFiles` and more), but it registers none of them. In BxAgents an agent gets them by listing them **and** naming the folders they may use in `toolOptions.bxai.allowedPaths`:

```yaml
tools:
  - readFile@bxai
  - listDirectory@bxai
toolOptions:
  bxai:
    allowedPaths:
      - tmp                  # the system temp folder
      - cwd                  # the folder the agent is started from
      - /data/reports        # or an absolute path
```

* **Each agent gets its own tools, locked to its own folders.** A path outside them is refused (`..` tricks included), and the tools are never put in the shared registry where another agent could pick them up.
* **No folders, no tools.** The tools exist only when `allowedPaths` is set, and an empty list is a build error, because bx-ai reads an empty list as "any path". Listing `readFile@bxai` with no `allowedPaths` fails with a message saying so.
* `now@bxai`, `httpGet@bxai`, `webSearch@bxai` and the rest of bx-ai's registered tools keep working as before, with or without `toolOptions.bxai`. `*@bxai` includes the file tools once `allowedPaths` is set.
* An entry may be `${env.NAME}` to take a folder from the environment.
* `bxAgents new` can write all of this for you: see [the new wizard](/next/guides/new-wizard/index.html).

## Notes

An agent can keep short notes: things about the user ("prefers short answers") and things about its own work ("the repo uses Gradle"). They are off until the block is there:

```yaml
notes: {}
```

```yaml
notes:
  provider: sqlite        # built in. Or a class implementing INotesProvider
  user:  { limit: 1400 }  # characters of user notes that go into the prompt
  agent: { limit: 2200 }  # characters of agent notes
  tool: true              # give the agent the remember and forget tools (default true)
  approveForget: true     # a person approves what the agent forgets (default true)
```

|       Key       | Default  |                                                                                                                                   Notes                                                                                                                                    |
|-----------------|----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `provider`      | `sqlite` | `sqlite` keeps one row per note in the [shared chat database](/next/conventions/web-ui/index.html#the-sqlite-store). Any other value is the name of a class that implements `INotesProvider` and is created with `( config, agentName )`, for a notes service of your own. |
| `user.limit`    | 1400     | Characters of notes about the user. Each user has their own.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `agent.limit`   | 2200     | Characters of notes about the agent's work. Shared by everyone who talks to it.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `tool`          | `true`   | `remember` (save or replace a note) and `forget` (remove one). Without them the notes are read-only for the agent and a person manages them.                                                                                                                               |
| `approveForget` | `true`   | A run that wants to `forget` stops for [approval](/next/cli-reference/index.html#chat), like any tool that needs it. Saving a note needs none.                                                                                                                             |

How it works:

* Both scopes go into the system prompt as short lists, oldest first, within their limits. They are read once per conversation, so the prompt stays the same turn to turn (a provider's prompt cache keeps working) and a note saved now shows from the next conversation.
* A note is one line of at most 500 characters. Nothing is dropped silently: a note that does not fit the limit is refused, and the agent is told how full the notes are so it can replace or forget an older one.
* **Who a user is** : in `bxAgents chat` it is the operating system user (`--user=NAME` changes it); on a server it is the name of the [access token](/next/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#access-tokens-for-a-deployed-agent) the caller used, or `api` when the route is open. The agent scope belongs to the agent's `name`.
* The terminal chat, the web chat and the server share one file, `data/chat.db` (see [the SQLite store](/next/conventions/web-ui/index.html#the-sqlite-store)).

Manage them yourself with `/remember` and `/notes` in [`chat`](/next/cli-reference/index.html#chat), with [`bxAgents notes`](/next/cli-reference/index.html#notes) from a shell, or over HTTP through the [run-control routes](/next/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#run-control).

## Instructions

The agent's instructions are its system prompt. Put them in an `instructions.md` beside `Agent.yaml`, the usual choice because the file is plain Markdown and easy to edit:

    my-agent/
    ├── Agent.yaml
    └── instructions.md

For a short prompt you can write them inline instead:

```yaml
name: greeter
model: openai/gpt-5
instructions: |
  You greet people by name.
  Keep it to one sentence.
```

If both exist, **`instructions.md` wins** - the file is the more deliberate choice, so a stray `instructions:` line cannot override it. If neither exists, `build` fails and says so.

## Environments

`environments` holds overrides keyed by environment name. It is the YAML spelling of the environment-override methods (`production()`) an `Agent.bx` can declare:

```yaml
name: support
model: openai/gpt-5

environments:
  production:
    model: openai/gpt-5-mini
  staging:
    description: Staging copy
```

The active environment is chosen with this precedence, highest first:

1. the `--environment` CLI flag (`bxAgents build --environment=production`)
2. the `BX_AGENTS_ENV` environment variable
3. `development`

Only the block for the active environment is applied, on top of the top-level settings; keys it does not mention are left alone. Each block accepts the same keys as the top level, except `environments` itself.

`bxAgents test` builds against the `test` environment, which is why a scaffolded project carries a `test` block pointing at the `mock` provider: its tests need no API key or network access.
> **Note**
>
> An `Agent.yaml` cannot compute its environment. The `detectEnvironment()` method described under [Environment overrides](/next/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#environment-overrides) needs code, so a project that needs it uses an `Agent.bx`.

The overrides then merge with `boxlang.json`, `boxlang-{environment}.json`, `miniserver.json` and `miniserver-{environment}.json` exactly as described in [Merge semantics](/next/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#merge-semantics).

## Requirements

Reading YAML needs the `bx-yaml` module, **1.1.0 or later** . BxAgents bundles it, so there is nothing to install. Global YAML tags (such as `!!java.io.File`) are rejected, so a cloned project's `Agent.yaml` cannot make the build instantiate arbitrary Java classes.

## YAML or Agent.bx?

|                         Use                         |                                                                   When                                                                   |
|-----------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `Agent.yaml`                                        | The agent is configuration: a name, a model, instructions, memory, subagents. This is almost every agent.                                |
| [`Agent.bx`](/next/conventions/agent-bx/index.html) | The definition itself needs code: hooks, dynamic instructions, tools registered in code, an overridden method, or `detectEnvironment()`. |

You can start with YAML and switch later: create the `Agent.bx`, move the settings across, and delete the `Agent.yaml`.
